question: Which channelizing device in Figure 6K-1 is illustrated with three horizontal striped rails?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The Type 3 Barricade is the channelizing device in Figure 6K-1 that is illustrated with three horizontal striped rails (each rail 8 to 12 inches high, at least 4 feet long, with the top of the barricade a minimum of 5 feet above the ground). By comparison, the Type 1 Barricade has one rail and the Type 2 Barricade has two rails. Standards (mandatory): - "Designs of various channelizing devices shall be as shown in Figure 6K-1. All channelizing devices shall be crashworthy (see definition in Section 1C.02)." - Per the figure notes: "Rail stripe widths shall be 6 inches, except that 4-inch wide stripes may be used if rail lengths are less than 36 inches. The sides of barricades facing traffic shall have retroreflective rail faces." Options (permitted): - Warning lights on barricades are optional, as noted in Figure 6K-1. - Channelizing devices such as barricades "may be used for general traffic control purposes such as adding emphasis to reversible lane delineation, channelizing lines, islands, pedestrian facilities, or bicycle facilities." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 6K-1 depicts the TYPE 3 BARRICADE with three horizontal orange-and-white striped rails (8 to 12 inches each, 4 ft MIN rail length, 5 ft MIN overall height), whereas the Type 1 and Type 2 Barricades are shown with one and two rails, respectively. Citations: - Section 6K.01 Standard §1 (p.815) - Section 6K.02 Support §1 (p.817) - Section 3I.01 Option §1 (p.632) - Figure 6K-1 (p.815)
